title: Cardhu: The Women Behind Johnnie Walker's Malt
description: Helen Cumming made whisky without a licence on a Speyside hill farm. Her daughter-in-law Elizabeth rebuilt the distillery, sold its old stills to the man starting Glenfiddich, and set the terms when her family sold it to John Walker & Sons in 1893. Four pours, from Cardhu's own malt to the 2003 row over its name.

pours.name: Cardhu 12 Year Old
pours.notes: The distillery's own single malt. Diageo calls Cardhu a key malt in Johnnie Walker; taste it on its own first.

pours.name: Glenfiddich 12 Year Old
pours.notes: William Grant started Glenfiddich in 1886 with the old stills and equipment he bought from Cardow for about £120.

pours.name: Johnnie Walker Black Label
pours.notes: The firm that bought Cardow in 1893, its first distillery. Go back to glass 1 and look for the Cardhu in it.

pours.name: Johnnie Walker Green Label
pours.notes: Malts from several distilleries and no grain, the same kind of whisky as the 2003 Cardhu Pure Malt. Sold as Johnnie Walker Pure Malt until 2004.
